name: Kommerell Diverticulum

criteria.description: Identification of a saccular or fusiform aneurysmal dilation at the origin of an aberrant subclavian artery on imaging
Presence of an aberrant right or left subclavian artery arising from a diverticulum of the aortic arch
Clinical symptoms attributable to esophageal or tracheal compression by the diverticulum

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Imaging confirmation of Kommerell diverticulum with aberrant subclavian artery origin
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily radiological; symptomatic presentation supports clinical relevance

pathognomonic.notes: Difficulty swallowing due to esophageal compression
High-pitched wheezing sound caused by airway obstruction

common.symptomName: Chest pain related to aneurysmal dilation
searchTerms: chest pain from enlarged blood vessel
pain related to aneurysm in chest

common.notes: Persistent cough due to airway irritation

common.symptomName: Hoarseness from recurrent laryngeal nerve irritation
common.notes: Voice changes secondary to nerve compression
searchTerms: voice changes due to recurrent laryngeal nerve

occasional.notes: Coldness or numbness in the affected arm
searchTerms: symptoms of poor blood flow in arms
reduced circulation causing arm pain or numbness

occasional.notes: Due to airway compression and impaired clearance

rare.symptomName: Syncope due to vascular steal phenomena
searchTerms: fainting due to blood flow diversion
passing out caused by blood flow issues

rare.notes: Coughing up blood due to erosion or rupture

imaging: CT angiography showing saccular aneurysmal dilation at origin of aberrant subclavian artery
MRI angiography demonstrating Kommerell diverticulum morphology
other: Bronchoscopy may show external tracheal compression
Echocardiography to assess associated cardiac anomalies

distinguishingFeatures: Complete vascular ring encircling trachea and esophagus
Aneurysm not associated with aberrant subclavian artery
Usually involves ascending or descending aorta
Lack of esophageal or tracheal compression symptoms

redFlags: Sudden onset severe chest or back pain
Signs of airway obstruction or respiratory distress
Evidence of aortic rupture or dissection
references: Backer CL, Mavroudis C. Kommerell diverticulum: a comprehensive review. Semin Thorac Cardiovasc Surg Pediatr Card Surg Annu. 2010;13(1):28-34.
Fukui T, et al. Kommerell diverticulum: clinical features and surgical outcomes. Ann Thorac Surg. 2015;99(6):1962-1967.
